Date: August 14, 2026

**RE: Urgent Member Appeal for Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Emerson Jennings
*   **Member ID:** W359699103
*   **Date of Birth:** [Patient Date of Birth]
*   **Patient Address:** [Patient Address]
*   **Patient Phone Number:** [Patient Phone Number]
*   **Prior Authorization Reference Number:** POC-3A565C0679-61883
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion
*   **Procedure Code:** CPT 22612
*   **Requesting Physician:** [First Name] Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my lumbar spine fusion (CPT 22612), issued on August 9, 2026. The denial letter states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. This determination is clinically incorrect and directly contradicted by my detailed medical records. 

My case meets and exceeds all medical necessity criteria outlined in the governing clinical policy: **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery** (Effective July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027). Below, my medical history is directly mapped to the plan's specific requirements to demonstrate complete clinical compliance.

### 1. Evidence of Severe, Chronic Symptoms
The policy requires:
> "Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months"

My records document 24 months of progressive lower back and bilateral leg pain that is unrelieved by rest. This chronic pain causes severe neurogenic claudication, which profoundly limits my daily activities. Currently, I cannot stand or walk for more than 10 minutes before experiencing severe leg pain and heaviness that forces me to stop. These symptoms are temporarily relieved only by sitting. Clinical examinations also show diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.

### 2. Proof of a Completed Multimodality Conservative Treatment Program
The policy dictates that:
> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

My records confirm that I completed a comprehensive, concurrent multimodality conservative treatment program consisting of the following plan-approved components:

*   **Active Modality ("Physical therapy"):** From April 1, 2026, to June 10, 2026, I completed 10 weeks and 20 sessions of supervised physical therapy at `[Physical Therapy Facility Name]` focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. This is fully documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Inactive Modality ("Medications (e.g., NSAIDs, steroids, analgesics)"):** I was prescribed and took therapeutic doses of NSAIDs for 6 months to manage my spinal pain, which provided inadequate relief.
*   **Inactive Modality ("Injections (e.g., epidural steroid injection, selective nerve root block)"):** On March 21, 2026, I underwent a lumbar corticosteroid injection performed by `[Injection Provider/Facility]`, which provided only three weeks of partial relief before my baseline pain returned.

My clinical course clearly demonstrates a compliant, dual-category multimodality approach targeting my lumbar spine.

### 3. Documented Failure of Conservative Treatment Within 6 Months
The plan's guideline states that surgery is appropriate upon:
> "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"

The guideline further defines this failure as:
> "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment"

The physical therapy discharge note dated June 10, 2026, as well as Dr. Reyes' clinical notes, explicitly document that despite completing 10 weeks of physical therapy (far exceeding the 6-week requirement) within the last six months of the surgical request, I experienced a complete "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment". My pain, sensory deficits, and functional limitations persist at an unacceptable level.

### 4. Objective Clinical and Radiographic Findings
The policy requires imaging studies corresponding to clinical findings and the presence of at least one specified clinical condition, including:
> "Spondylolisthesis"
> "Evidence of segmental instability"

My lumbar spine MRI and flexion-extension radiographs, performed on July 8, 2026, at `[Imaging Center]`, show a Grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation (confirming segmental instability) and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. These objective findings correlate exactly with my symptoms of neurogenic claudication and L5 sensory deficits.

### 5. Exclusion of Contraindications
I do not have any active infections, untreated substance use disorders, or contraindications to surgery. I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29, making me an excellent surgical candidate.

### Conclusion
I have tried and failed over 6 months of active and inactive conservative therapies, including a recent 10-week course of physical therapy, NSAIDs, and an injection, none of which resulted in functional recovery. Because I meet every single criterion set forth under **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766**, I request that you reverse this denial immediately and authorize CPT 22612 so that I may receive this medically necessary surgery.

Please contact Dr. Reyes' office at `[Provider Phone Number]` or me at the number above if you require any additional information. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Jennings
